newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spanish army officer killed in apparent ETA attack.
newsitem.headline: Spanish army officer killed in apparent ETA attack.

text.p: A Spanish army officer was shot and killed by a woman in an apparent attack by Basque separatist guerrillas ETA in northeast Madrid on Wednesday, officials said.
A car exploded shortly afterwards near a shopping centre in the same neighbourhood and slightly injured a member of the Royal Guard who was passing by.
Police said the woman and a male partner may have used the car and destroyed it afterward, a method commonly used by ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom).
"It has all the signs of being an ETA action, although it's too soon to confirm," Madrid's mayor Jose Maria Alvarez del Manzano told journalists.

An interior ministry spokeswoman told Reuters that the attack happened at 3.15 p.m. (1415 GMT) when a young woman and a man approached Lt-Colonel Jesus Cuesta, 60, as he got out of his car to enter his house.
The woman fired twice, shooting Cuesta in the head and jaw, and the man fired at the officer's driver without hitting him.
Cuesta died on the way to hospital.

Officials said his death, if confirmed as ETA's work, would mark the first separatist assassination this year and the first in the capital city since an ETA gunman shot and killed an ex-constitutional court judge last February.
The group has killed about 800 people since 1968 when it started a campaign of shootings, bombings and kidnappings to bring about Basque independence.
"We know that this is not a short-term battle," Spain's Interior Minister Jaime Mayor Oreja told journalists after visiting the injured Royal Guardsman in hospital.
"At times like these, Spanish society has to know where the main responsibility lies...We know we have to work hard in the fight against terrorism."
Oreja warned on Tuesday that ETA could be planning an attack in retaliation for recent arrests of violent youth followers of the separatist group.

Spain's security forces were placed on alert on Tuesday after five grenades were launched against Madrid's Barajas airport and a series of small bombs exploded at electricity towers in northern Spain on Monday.
